Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with dry, itchy skin for the past few days, associated with recent work stress.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I've been really stressed at work for the past few days... And, I've realised that I've got, really dry itchy skin.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The dry, itchy, red skin is located on her arms and hands.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: All over my arms, um, and my hands mainly... so my skin's quite red

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms started a few days ago, after the patient went swimming.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I think it started a few days ago... I went swimming a few days ago... did your symptoms start after you went swimming? Uh, yes, .

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has been using coconut butter with no improvement.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I'm using coconut butter for the past few days... the coconut butter hasn't helped, with the itch? No, .

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies spots, fever, or sweating.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I don't have any spots, and no fever , and I'm not sweating either.
do you feel generally run-down? Do you feel tired? Uh, yeah, I think I have been, quite tired.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient's appetite, eating, drinking, bowel movements, and urination are normal.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I've been drinking, and eating as normal... Are your bowels working OK? Yeah... your waterworks are uh, all OK? Yep.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has no history of skin problems like eczema or dermatitis.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: in terms of your medical history, there's no, problems of skin problems in the past, things like eczema or, um, dermatitis? Uh, no

Past_Medical_History.source_text: I think, um, I might be lactose intolerant.

Medications.content: Patient takes the contraceptive pill Microgynon.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.content: Patient has no known medication allergies.
Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Food allergies? Medication allergies? (Implied no to medications)

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is 26 years old, lives alone, and works as a teacher.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: my name's Itha, and I'm twenty six... it's just me... I work as a teacher.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient has been experiencing significant stress at work due to long hours and difficult students.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I think the kids have been really annoying these days... And, I've been working really long hours.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and does not use recreational drugs.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I don't smoke... Do you drink much in the way of alcohol? Uh, no... Recreational drugs? No.

Assessment.source_text: I wonder whether you may have something called dermatitis.

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be applied twice daily (BD).
Advised to use emollients regularly (up to four times a day - QDS) for dry skin.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: something called emollients, which can help with the dry, dry skin... that's something you just need to kind of paste on, uh, on to your skin, uh, , throughout the day

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommended trying over-the-counter antihistamines like Piriton or Loratadine for itching.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: you can also try antihistamines, so you can get things over the counter, Piriton, Loratadine, they can sometimes help with the itchiness.

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review next week if symptoms are not better or are worsening.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: if it's still not getting better, come back and see me next week, and we can have another look again, at your symptoms.
